content: There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you.
author: Maya Angelou
sourceWork: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (1969)
story: After enduring traumatic childhood abuse in Stamps, Arkansas, Maya Angelou spent nearly five years in voluntary muteness, believing her voice had the power to kill. It was through literature, poetry, and the patient encouragement of teacher Bertha Flowers that she slowly reclaimed her voice. Writing her autobiography decades later, she reflected on the toxic psychological pressure of silence: unexpressed truth festering within the human spirit creates an agony far worse than the vulnerability of speaking out.
reflectionPrompt: What experience, truth, or creative vision have you held inside out of fear or hesitation, and what would it feel like to finally give it expression?
